hints.text: A two-digit multiplier can be split into tens and ones. Multiply by each part, then put the parts together.
Split $27$ into $20 + 7$. Find $38 \times 20$ and $38 \times 7$, then add the two partial products.
$38 \times 20 = 760$ and $38 \times 7 = 266$, and $760 + 266 = 1026$, so the product is $1026$.

explanation: Split $27$ into $20 + 7$, because multiplying by each part separately is easier than doing it all at once.
Multiply by the tens part: $38 \times 20 = 760$, which is $38 \times 2$ with a zero attached.
Multiply by the ones part: $38 \times 7 = 266$, since $30 \times 7 = 210$ and $8 \times 7 = 56$.
Add the partial products to cover all $27$ groups: $760 + 266 = 1026$, so $38 \times 27 = 1026$.
